title: Pauli Spectrum and Stabilizer Rényi Entropy in Gapless Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases
abstract: Quantum entanglement is widely used as a diagnostic of topological phases of matter. Beyond entanglement, non-stabilizerness captures a distinct aspect of quantum many-body states by quantifying their distance from the manifold of stabilizer states. In this work, we study the stabilizer Rényi entropy in symmetry protected topological (SPT) phases, including both gapped SPT, non-intrinsically gapless SPT, and intrinsically gapless SPT phases. Under symmetry preserving perturbations, we find numerically that the stabilizer Rényi entropy exhibits an extremum near the phase transition. However, the stabilizer Rényi entropy alone cannot distinguish different SPT phases. In contrast, the Pauli spectrum reveals a characteristic crossing structure at the transition point. This crossing reflects the exchange of dominant Pauli-string correlations associated with the non-local string order parameters of the two topological distinct phases. For gapped SPT and non-intrinsically gapless SPT phases, the crossing structure can be understood from a local-unitary duality that maps the Pauli spectrum between the two phases. For intrinsically gapless SPT phases, such a local-unitary mapping is absent. Instead, we find that the Pauli spectrum mapping is generated by a non-invertible duality transformation. These results show that although the stabilizer Rényi entropy provides only a coarse diagnostic of phase transitions, the Pauli spectrum contains finer information about the exchange of string order sectors. Our findings demonstrate that quantum magic offers a complementary perspective for characterizing both gapped and gapless SPT phases.
summary: This work introduces the Pauli spectrum as a superior diagnostic tool compared to stabilizer Rényi entropy for characterizing Symmetry-Protected Topological phases. By analyzing how the Pauli correlations change across phase transitions using duality mappings, the authors demonstrate that this method can resolve subtle differences between gapped and gapless topological orders in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop advanced quantum diagnostics beyond standard entanglement measures to characterize Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) phases.
main_result: While the stabilizer Rényi entropy provides only a coarse diagnostic, the Pauli spectrum reveals a characteristic crossing structure at phase transitions, offering finer information about string order sector exchange.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis of quantum correlation functions using the Pauli spectrum and calculating the Stabilizer Rényi Entropy (SRE) for various SPT models.
model_or_system: The research analyzes general SPT phases, including gapped, non-intrinsically gapless, and intrinsically gapless types. Specific models include a 1D cluster SPT model and the Cluster Ising Model.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy (SRE), Pauli spectrum (the full probability distribution of Pauli strings), and the crossing structure observed in the Pauli spectrum at phase transitions.
important_parameters: The coupling constants ($h, g_0, g_1, g_2$) defining the Hamiltonian; system size ($L$); and the Rényi parameter ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on pure ground states and utilizes duality transformations (local-unitary or non-invertible Kramers-Wannier type) to map between different topological phases.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the calculated $\mathcal{M}_2$ (SRE proxy) and the Pauli spectrum for cluster SPT models, showing distinct red (SPT) vs. blue (trivial) correlations; other figures show convergence checks for these observables in various model regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares SRE against the Pauli spectrum across different classes of SPT phases (gapped, non-intrinsically gapless, intrinsically gapless), detailing how duality transformations govern the observed spectral changes at critical points.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for using local correlation measurements (Pauli strings) to distinguish between subtle topological orders in strongly correlated quantum materials, which is highly relevant to understanding exotic electronic states.
